html:
Malta became independent from Britain on 21 September 1964, with the British queen still as head of state. It became a republic in 1974.

Under British rule since 1800 the islands lived largely from the naval dockyards. After the Second World War, Maltese parties debated full union with Britain, which a 1956 referendum backed but which fell through, and then independence. The Nationalist leader George Borg Olivier negotiated it.

The Labour leader Dom Mintoff then made Malta a republic and closed the last British base in 1979, a date marked as Freedom Day. Malta joined the European Union in 2004 and the euro in 2008. Its economy turned to tourism, finance and online gambling. Many Maltese had emigrated, to Australia above all.
sum: Malta became independent from Britain on 21 September 1964, with the British queen still as head of state. It became a republic in 1974.
